bull.b: Strong revenue and gross-profit growth indicate improving operating scale and enhanced earnings capacity. The higher gross margin provides more cash generation per ounce and may support reinvestment, while demonstrating that stronger realized pricing is translating into meaningful operating leverage.

The How Mine expansion offers a tangible route to higher production capacity using an existing operation and infrastructure base. If commissioning and ramp-up proceed as planned, greater throughput can improve fixed-cost absorption and support a larger production platform into 2027.

A substantial increase in operating cash flow strengthens the company’s ability to fund mine development internally and reduces reliance on equity issuance for near-term initiatives. Reinvestment also indicates that cash generation is being directed toward expanding productive capacity.

bear.b: Persistently negative equity weakens the capital structure even though absolute debt is relatively low. It leaves less balance-sheet resilience if operating performance deteriorates, limits financing flexibility, and increases the importance of sustained positive cash generation from the mines.

The large working-capital deficit and modest cash balance create ongoing pressure to convert production into cash and maintain access to financing. Near-term obligations, including borrowings due within one year, could constrain development spending if cash flows or operating execution weaken.

Reduced production guidance and higher expected all-in sustaining costs point to weaker operating efficiency and less margin protection. The delayed mill ramp, lower grades, and fixed-cost absorption pressure make future profitability more dependent on successful execution and sustained gold prices.
